testName: IISER IAT - Electromagnetic Induction & AC Circuits: Advanced (20 Questions)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conducting rod of length L rotates with angular velocity ω about one end in a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to the plane of rotation. The emf between the ends is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Consider element dr at distance r from pivot. Velocity v = ωr.
Step 2: Motional emf de = Bvdr = Bωr dr.
Step 3: Total emf: ε = ∫₀ᴸ Bωr dr = Bω[L²/2] = ½BωL².
Step 4: This is the principle of homopolar generator (Faraday disk).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A square loop of side a and resistance R is pulled out of a uniform magnetic field B (perpendicular to loop) with constant velocity v. The power required is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: As loop exits, flux changes. Rate of change of area in field = av.
Step 2: Induced emf: ε = B(av) = Bav. Current: I = Bav/R.
Step 3: Magnetic force on current-carrying side: F = BIa = B(Bav/R)a = B²a²v/R.
Step 4: Power: P = Fv = B²a²v²/R. Alternatively: P = I²R = (Bav/R)²R = B²a²v²/R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A solenoid with inductance L carries current I. The energy stored is U = ½LI². If the current is increased to 2I and inductance halved (by removing core), the new energy is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Original: U = ½LI².
Step 2: New: L' = L/2, I' = 2I.
Step 3: U' = ½(L/2)(2I)² = ½(L/2)(4I²) = ½ × 2LI² = LI² = 2 × (½LI²) = 2U.
Step 4: Energy doubles despite halving inductance because current dependence is quadratic.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an LR circuit with time constant τ = L/R, the current grows as I = I₀(1 - e^(-t/τ)). The time at which current reaches half maximum is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Set I = I₀/2: I₀/2 = I₀(1 - e^(-t/τ)).
Step 2: ½ = 1 - e^(-t/τ) → e^(-t/τ) = ½ → -t/τ = ln(½) = -ln2.
Step 3: Therefore t = τln2 ≈ 0.693τ.
Step 4: This is the half-life for current growth, analogous to radioactive decay.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A transformer has primary turns N₁, secondary turns N₂. The primary voltage is V₁, secondary load is R. The equivalent resistance seen by primary is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Voltage ratio: V₂/V₁ = N₂/N₁. Current ratio: I₂/I₁ = N₁/N₂.
Step 2: Secondary: V₂ = I₂R. Primary sees: V₁ = I₁R_eq.
Step 3: R_eq = V₁/I₁ = (V₁/V₂)(V₂/I₁) = (N₁/N₂)(I₂R/I₁) = (N₁/N₂)(N₁/N₂)R = R(N₁/N₂)².
Step 4: Impedance transforms as square of turns ratio. Step-down transformer (N₂ < N₁) reflects reduced impedance to primary.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An AC circuit has voltage V = V₀sin(ωt) applied to series RL circuit. The phase angle φ by which current lags voltage satisfies:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Impedance Z = √(R² + (ωL)²).
Step 2: Phase angle: tanφ = X_L/R = ωL/R (A is correct).
Step 3: Also sinφ = X_L/Z = ωL/√(R² + ω²L²) (C is correct).
Step 4: Both relations describe the same phase angle. For purely inductive circuit, φ = 90°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A series LCR circuit is at resonance. The impedance is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Impedance Z = √(R² + (ωL - 1/ωC)²).
Step 2: At resonance: ω₀L = 1/ω₀C → reactances cancel.
Step 3: Z_min = √(R² + 0) = R.
Step 4: Current is maximum at resonance, limited only by resistance. This is the principle of tuning circuits.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The quality factor Q of a series resonant circuit is defined as ω₀L/R. It can also be expressed as:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: At resonance: ω₀ = 1/√(LC) → ω₀L = 1/ω₀C.
Step 2: So Q = ω₀L/R = 1/(ω₀CR). (A and equivalent form)
Step 3: Bandwidth Δω = R/L (half-power frequencies). So Q = ω₀/(R/L) = ω₀L/R = ω₀/Δω.
Step 4: Higher Q means sharper resonance, narrower bandwidth, better selectivity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal inductor (no resistance) is connected to AC source. The average power consumed is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In inductor, current lags voltage by 90°.
Step 2: Instantaneous power: P(t) = V(t)I(t) = V₀sin(ωt) × I₀sin(ωt - 90°) = V₀I₀sin(ωt)(-cos(ωt)) = -½V₀I₀sin(2ωt).
Step 3: Average of sin(2ωt) over full cycle is zero.
Step 4: No net power dissipated; energy is stored in magnetic field during one quarter cycle and returned during next.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A metal disc of radius R rotates with angular velocity ω in a uniform magnetic field B parallel to the axis. The emf between center and rim is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: This is a homopolar generator (Faraday disk).
Step 2: Consider radial element dr at radius r. Velocity v = ωr perpendicular to B.
Step 3: Motional emf de = Bvdr = Bωr dr. Integrate: ε = ∫₀ᴿ Bωr dr = ½BωR².
Step 4: Despite continuous rotation, steady DC emf is generated (unlike alternator).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a mutual inductance setup, coil 1 has current I₁ changing at rate dI₁/dt. The induced emf in coil 2 is ε₂ = -M(dI₁/dt). The mutual inductance M:
options: Depends on geometry and relative position
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Mutual inductance depends on number of turns, size, shape, and relative orientation and distance between coils.
Step 2: Neumann formula proves reciprocity: M₁₂ = M₂₁ = M.
Step 3: Unit: [M] = [ε]/[dI/dt] = V/(A/s) = V·s/A = H (henry).
Step 4: All statements are fundamental properties of mutual inductance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conducting rod of length L slides with velocity v on two parallel rails separated by L, connected by resistance R. A uniform magnetic field B is perpendicular to the plane. The mechanical power required equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Induced emf: ε = BLv. Current: I = BLv/R.
Step 2: Magnetic force on rod: F = BIL = B(BLv/R)L = B²L²v/R.
Step 3: Mechanical power: P_mech = Fv = B²L²v²/R.
Step 4: Electrical power: P_elec = I²R = (BLv/R)²R = B²L²v²/R. Energy conservation requires P_mech = P_elec.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An AC circuit has resistor R, inductor L, and capacitor C in series. At frequency ω, the power factor is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Power factor = cosφ = R/Z where Z is impedance.
Step 2: Z = √(R² + X²) where X = ωL - 1/ωC is net reactance.
Step 3: tanφ = X/R = (ωL - 1/ωC)/R.
Step 4: All three forms are equivalent expressions for power factor. At resonance, φ = 0, power factor = 1 (maximum).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Passage: A superconducting loop of inductance L is cooled below its critical temperature in the presence of an external magnetic flux Φ_ext. The flux through the loop is quantized.

Question 1: The flux quantum Φ₀ is given by:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In superconductors, Cooper pairs (charge 2e) are the charge carriers.
Step 2: Flux quantization condition: ∮(mv + qA)·dl = nℏ where q = 2e for Cooper pairs.
Step 3: This leads to Φ = n(h/2e) = nΦ₀ where Φ₀ = h/(2e) ≈ 2.068 × 10⁻¹⁵ Wb.
Step 4: This is half the flux quantum for normal electrons (h/e), reflecting Cooper pairing.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Using the same superconducting loop, if the external flux Φ_ext is slowly changed, the induced current I in the loop satisfies:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Total flux through loop: Φ_total = Φ_ext + LI (self-flux).
Step 2: Flux quantization: Φ_total = nΦ₀ where n is integer.
Step 3: Therefore: LI + Φ_ext = nΦ₀.
Step 4: As Φ_ext changes, current I adjusts to maintain fluxoid quantization, with n changing by discrete jumps when energetically favorable.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A conducting loop falls under gravity through a region of uniform horizontal magnetic field. The terminal velocity is reached when:
options: Gravitational potential loss equals heat generated
questions.explanation:
Step 1: As loop falls, changing flux induces current, creating magnetic force opposing motion (Lenz's law).
Step 2: At terminal velocity v_t: magnetic force upward = weight downward (A).
Step 3: Power balance: mgv_t = I²R (gravitational power input = resistive dissipation), which is equivalent to C.
Step 4: Both mechanical equilibrium (A) and energy conservation (C) describe terminal velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a series RLC circuit, the resonance frequency ω₀ = 1/√(LC). If L is increased by 1% and C decreased by 1%, the percentage change in ω₀ is approximately:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: ω₀ = (LC)^(-1/2). ln(ω₀) = -½(lnL + lnC).
Step 2: Differential: dω₀/ω₀ = -½(dL/L + dC/C).
Step 3: With dL/L = +0.01 and dC/C = -0.01: dω₀/ω₀ = -½(0.01 - 0.01) = 0.
Step 4: To first order, the changes cancel. Second order effect is -(0.01)²/4 = -0.0025% (negligible).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An inductor with inductance L and internal resistance R is connected to DC source V. The time constant for current growth is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Circuit equation: V = L(dI/dt) + IR.
Step 2: This is first-order linear ODE with solution I = (V/R)(1 - e^(-t/τ)).
Step 3: Time constant τ = L/R has dimensions of time: [L]/[R] = [V·s/A]/[V/A] = [s].
Step 4: After time τ, current reaches ~63% of final value V/R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A transformer has efficiency η = 90%. If input power is 1000 W at 200 V, and output voltage is 100 V, the output current is approximately:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Input power P_in = 1000 W. Output power P_out = ηP_in = 0.9 × 1000 = 900 W.
Step 2: Output voltage V_out = 100 V.
Step 3: Output current I_out = P_out/V_out = 900/100 = 9 A.
Step 4: Input current I_in = P_in/V_in = 1000/200 = 5 A. Turns ratio N₁/N₂ = V₁/V₂ = 2, and I₂/I₁ = N₁/N₂ = 2 (ignoring losses), so I₂ = 10 A. With losses, slightly less: 9 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The skin depth δ in a conductor for electromagnetic wave of frequency ω is δ = √(2/(μσω)). At higher frequencies, the skin depth:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Skin depth δ ∝ 1/√ω.
Step 2: As ω increases, δ decreases: higher frequency fields penetrate less into conductor.
Step 3: This is why high frequency currents flow near surface (skin effect), increasing effective resistance.
Step 4: At ω → 0 (DC), δ → ∞ (uniform current distribution). At ω → ∞, δ → 0 (surface current only).
